# Code of conduct

Marquise is a small project, and people come to it from very different places: some build Android apps, some have
never opened a terminal and just want their TV back. Everyone gets the same patience.

## What we expect

- **Be kind and assume good faith.** A question that seems obvious is a sign the docs can be clearer.
- **Talk about the work, not the person.** Disagree with a change, a design or a decision freely, with reasons.
- **Help people get to an answer.** Point to the docs, ask what TV they have, show the command. A short "read the
  README" isn't help.
- **Respect people's time and privacy.** Never post someone's addresses, keys, logs or personal details without their
  consent. Remove your own before posting.
- **Write in English or Portuguese**, whichever is easier for you.

## What isn't accepted

- Harassment, insults, or demeaning remarks about anyone's identity, background, ability or level of experience.
- Sexual language or imagery, threats, or encouraging anyone to harm themselves or others.
- Publishing someone's private information.
- Spam, advertising, or using issues and pull requests to promote something unrelated.
- Repeating any of the above after being asked to stop.

## Where it applies

In this repository (issues, pull requests, discussions, reviews and commits), and anywhere someone speaks for the
project.

## Reporting

Reports go privately to the maintainer through [Report a vulnerability](https://github.com/vitoramaral10/marquise/security/advisories/new)
on GitHub (the *Security* tab). Start the title with **Conduct**. That form is the one private channel the project
has, and only the maintainer sees what is sent there. For something in plain view, you can also use GitHub's *Report
content* on the comment.

Every report is read, and the person reporting is never named without their consent.

## What happens

Depending on what happened and whether it repeats:

1. **A private note** saying what was wrong.
2. **A public warning**, with comments hidden or edited when needed.
3. **A temporary block** from the repository.
4. **A permanent block.**

Anything sent through the project can be removed, and so can any contribution that breaks this code.

This code takes its ideas from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/).
